name: TrailStopBelowLastHigherLow
quote: trailing a stop: As the trade becomes increasingly profitable, traders will often move, or trail, the protective stop... if they are long in a bull trend, every time the market moves to a new high, they might raise the protective stop to just below the most recent higher low.
description: For an open long, once a new swing high forms, move the protective stop up to just below the most recently confirmed higher swing low (mirror for shorts: below the most recent lower swing high).
pseudocode: SwingHigh[1] && lastSwingLow() > priorSwingLow(); stopPrice = lastSwingLow() - stopBufferTicks * tickSize
book_order_type: protective stop order, trailed on each new confirmed higher low

complexity.reason: needs the last two confirmed swing pivots plus position state

notes: Not the same as the catalog's dollar-based TrailingStop; this trails to a structural swing level.

name: TrailingStopBelowRecentStrongTrendBar
quote: Many traders who bought the bar 15 close might have raised their stops to below bar 17 once it closed because they would not have wanted the market to fall below such a strong bull trend bar.
description: While long, trail the protective stop to just below the low of the most recent large-range bull trend bar, instead of a fixed distance.
pseudocode: strongBarLow = low[k] for the most recent bar k where BullTrendBar[k] && (high[k] - low[k]) >= rangeMultiple * atr(atrLookback); low[0] <= strongBarLow - toleranceTicks * tickSize
book_order_type: resting stop-loss order

complexity.reason: must remember the most recent qualifying trend bar's low as cross-bar state

chapter_title: Example of How to Trade a Breakout

name: TrailingStopInMicroMeasuringGap
quote: many might have put their protective stops in the micro measuring gap created by the bar 17 breakout. The low of bar 18 was above the high of bar 16, and this gap is a sign of strength.
description: Trail the protective stop into the most recent micro measuring gap: a two-bar-apart gap where a bar's low sits above the high of the bar two bars earlier.
pseudocode: gapLow = low[g] for the most recent g where low[g] > high[g + 2]; low[0] <= gapLow - toleranceTicks * tickSize
book_order_type: resting stop-loss order

complexity.reason: variable-offset gap detection plus persisted state for the most recent gap found

chapter_title: Example of How to Trade a Breakout

name: RestingStopAboveSpikeHigh
quote: traders needed to place their worst-case entry buy stop orders above the spike high ... They needed to place a buy stop at one tick above the bar 19 high, in case the trend quickly resumed.
description: While flat or looking to enter with-trend during a strong spike, keep a resting buy stop one tick above the recent spike high active, so a sudden resumption is not missed even if no pullback entry ever triggers.
pseudocode: high[0] >= highest(high, spikeBars)[1]
book_order_type: buy stop one tick above the spike high

complexity.reason: a highest-high window

chapter_title: Example of How to Trade a Breakout

name: PullbackHitsBreakeven
quote: The pullback hits the breakeven stop.
description: Sign of weakness: the pullback trades back to the position's own entry price.
pseudocode: ctx.MarketPosition() > 0 && low[0] <= ctx.EntryPrice() + toleranceTicks * tickSize
book_order_type: n/a (breakout-failure signal; often coincides with a breakeven stop order)

complexity.reason: a single comparison against the position's entry price

chapter_title: Signs of Strength in a Breakout

name: BreakevenStopAfterProfitThreshold
quote: Once bar 14 hit five ticks above the long entry, many bulls moved their stops to breakeven
description: Once open profit reaches a fixed tick threshold, move the protective stop to the entry price.
pseudocode: ctx.MarketPosition() > 0 && ctx.OpenPositionProfit() >= profitThresholdTicks * tickSize * bigPointValue
book_order_type: move the resting stop-loss order to the entry price

complexity.reason: a single open-profit comparison against a fixed threshold

notes: Distinct from the catalog's ProfitProtector (a proportional-giveback trail): this is a one-time breakeven move triggered at a fixed profit level, not tied to a peak or a retracement ratio.

name: CandlestickTrapFade
quote: When you see these small-bodied big candles in a strong trend where there has yet to be a trend line break, you should get excited because they are great traps and therefore perfect short setups.
description: In an intact bear trend (no trend-line break yet), a large-range, small-bodied bar with a long tail against the trend (a classic bullish 'hammer'/reversal candle) is a trap; fade it by placing an entry stop right where the trapped counter-trend traders' protective stops sit (beyond the tail).
pseudocode: !majorTrendLineBroken && (minList(open[0], close[0]) - low[0]) >= tailFraction * (high[0] - low[0]) && abs(close[0] - open[0]) <= smallBodyFraction * (high[0] - low[0])
book_order_type: sell stop one tick below the trap bar's low

complexity.reason: the bar test itself is simple, but 'no trend line break yet' is a persistent trend-line-projection state

name: ProtectiveStopBelowEntryBarLow
quote: The low of the entry bar. If the market falls below the entry bar, it often does so in a strong bear trend bar, and the move down from there is usually big enough for at least a scalp.
description: Exit the long if price trades below the low of the bar on which the position was entered (a natural stop/failure level distinct from the signal bar).
pseudocode: low[0] < ctx.EntryBarLow() - toleranceTicks * tickSize
book_order_type: protective sell stop at the entry bar's low

complexity.reason: needs to remember the specific entry bar's low, not just the entry price

notes: ctx.EntryBarLow() is a new accessor; the engine currently exposes EntryPrice but not the entry bar's own low/high.
chapter_title: Failed Breakouts, Breakout Pullbacks, and Breakout Tests

name: BreakevenStopBuffer
quote: After an initial run, many traders will take partial profits and then place a breakeven stop on the balance... the trader might place a breakeven stop at 30 cents beyond the breakout, even though it would result in at least a 30 cent loss
description: Once the position has been profitable by at least triggerTicks, move the stop for the remainder of the position to entry price minus bufferTicks (a 'breakeven' stop that may still take a small loss).
pseudocode: ctx.MaxPositionProfit() >= triggerTicks * tickSize && low[0] <= ctx.EntryPrice() - bufferTicks * tickSize
book_order_type: breakeven-plus-buffer protective stop

complexity.reason: needs entry price plus the position's peak profit

notes: Distinct from ProfitProtector: the floor is fixed at (near) entry price rather than a retracement fraction of peak profit.
chapter_title: Failed Breakouts, Breakout Pullbacks, and Breakout Tests

name: TrailingStopBeyondFailedTestBar
quote: Once the market falls below the breakout test bar, move the protective stop to 1 cent above its high.
description: After a breakout-pullback test bar fails to violate the trade (price does not make a new extreme through it), move the protective stop just beyond that test bar's extreme.
pseudocode: testBarLow = mostRecentFailedTestBarLow(); stopPrice = testBarLow - toleranceTicks * tickSize; low[0] <= stopPrice
book_order_type: trailing protective stop beyond the last failed test bar

complexity.reason: needs to remember the most recent qualifying test bar's extreme

chapter_title: Failed Breakouts, Breakout Pullbacks, and Breakout Tests

name: ProtectiveStopBeyondSpikeStart
quote: the initial protective stop is usually beyond the beginning of the first move. For example, if there is a strong buy spike, then the initial protective stop is one tick below the low of the spike.
description: Exit the long if price trades below the low of the identified spike's start (a wider, spike-anchored alternative to a signal-bar or entry-bar stop).
pseudocode: low[0] < spikeStartLow - toleranceTicks * tickSize
book_order_type: protective sell stop beyond the start of the spike

complexity.reason: needs the spike's start bar remembered from R07-01

notes: Distinct from R05-14 (stop below the entry bar): here the reference is the spike's own start, which may be several bars before the entry.
chapter_title: Measured Moves Based on the Size of the First Leg (the Spike)

name: OwnEntryPriceRetest
quote: Entry price (breakout test).
description: The trader's own entry price is itself a magnet -- price commonly returns to test it, a natural place to move a stop to breakeven or add to a position.
pseudocode: abs(close[0] - ctx.EntryPrice()) <= toleranceTicks * tickSize
book_order_type: n/a (management trigger, e.g. move stop to breakeven)

complexity.reason: a direct position-state accessor

name: NotableBarOppositeExtreme
quote: Entry bar and signal bar protective stops. Entry price (breakout test). Huge trend bar opposite extreme (the low of a huge bull trend bar and the high of a huge bear trend bar).
description: Shared primitive: the opposite extreme of a recent notable bar (a huge/large trend bar, or a signal/entry bar) is where protective stops commonly rest and therefore a magnet in its own right.
pseudocode: extreme = low[k] where bar k is a recorded LargeTrendBar (bull) within recentBars; the level persists until tested
book_order_type: n/a (level construction)

complexity.reason: records one extreme off an already-classified bar and keeps it live for a window

name: StopRunPastNotableBarExtremeThenReverse
quote: It is fairly common for the market to work its way to those stops and then reverse back in the direction of the trend bar. ... The market reversed down off the bear inside bar that followed and formed a higher low, but not before running the protective stops below the low of the trend bar.
description: The market probes a few ticks past a NotableBarOppositeExtreme (running the protective stops resting there) and then closes back on the trend side of it -- a with-trend re-entry signal.
pseudocode: low[0] < extreme - runTicks * tickSize && close[0] > extreme
book_order_type: buy stop above the bar that closed back above the extreme (a bull reversal bar)

complexity.reason: needs the persisted notable-bar extreme plus a probe-and-close-back test

notes: Figure 10.1: bar 2 ran the stops below bar 1's low (a huge bull trend bar) and then reversed the market back up.

name: StopDistanceEqualsTargetDistance
quote: A move equal to the size of the required protective stop: if an Emini trade required you to use a 12-tick protective stop to avoid getting stopped out, expect the move to ultimately reach 12 ticks in your favor.
description: Exit target set at the same distance (in ticks) as the trade's initial protective stop, scaled by a multiple.
pseudocode: close[0] >= ctx.EntryPrice() + targetMultiple * stopDistanceTicks * tickSize
book_order_type: limit order at entry price plus the stop distance

complexity.reason: a fixed offset from the entry price

notes: stopDistanceTicks is a parameter here since the actual protective stop is signal-bar-dependent and set per placement; related to TakeProfitWithRatioStop but framed as a 1R target rather than a dollar amount.

name: TrailingStopBelowRecentSwingLow
quote: If the market makes a new high, they will raise their stops to below the most recent higher low.
description: In a bull trend, trail the protective stop to just below the most recent confirmed swing low each time a new trend high forms.
pseudocode: high[0] > highest(high, lookback)[1] -> stopPrice = lowestSwingLow(pivotStrength) - bufferTicks * tickSize
book_order_type: trailing protective stop order

complexity.reason: needs swing-pivot detection plus persistence of the trailed stop level

notes: Not TrailingStop from the catalog (that trails by a dollar/ATR amount off peak profit); this trails to a structural swing level instead.
chapter_title: Part III: Pullbacks: Trends Converting to Trading Ranges

name: TightenStopToEntryBarIfTrendBar
quote: After the entry bar closes, the stop is moved to one tick below the entry bar if it is a trend bar. If it is a small bar, don't tighten the stop until there is a trend bar in your direction.
description: Stop-management primitive: once the entry bar (the bar that triggered the breakout fill) closes, tighten the protective stop to one tick below its low only if that bar is itself a trend bar; otherwise keep the original signal-bar stop until a later trend bar forms in the trade's direction.
pseudocode: onEntryBarClose: if isTrendBar(entryBar, bodyFraction) then stopPrice = low[entryBar] - stopOffsetTicks * tickSize; else keep prior stopPrice until the first later bar i with isTrendBar(i, bodyFraction) && close[i] > open[i], then stopPrice = low[i] - stopOffsetTicks * tickSize
book_order_type: trailing protective stop, tightened bar by bar under the rule above

complexity.reason: cross-bar state tracking which bar is 'the entry bar' and scanning forward for the first qualifying trend bar

chapter_title: Double Top Bear Flags and Double Bottom Bull Flags

name: WiderSwingStopWhenNoMaCloseBreak
quote: Look at the moving average. There were no closes below it after the initial bull spike to bar 10, so do not use a tight stop out of fear of losing a tick or two on your trade.
description: Stop-management filter: keep a wider swing-position protective stop (rather than a tight breakeven stop) as long as there has been no bar closing on the wrong side of the moving average since the current leg began.
pseudocode: barsSinceLegStart >= minBars && !exists i in [0, barsSinceLegStart): close[i] < ema(emaLength)[i]  -> keep the wider (structural) stop instead of breakeven
book_order_type: n/a (stop-management guidance)

complexity.reason: needs a scan since the leg's start plus the EMA

chapter_title: Double Top Bear Flags and Double Bottom Bull Flags

name: BuyStopAboveFirstCloseBelowMaBar
quote: a trader should be ready tomorrow to buy the first close below the moving average, and then buy again above the first moving average gap bar below the moving average.
description: In a strong bull trend, buy a stop above the high of the first bar to close below the moving average since the trend began.
pseudocode: isFirstCloseBelowMa(emaLength) && close[0] > close[1]  (entry trigger: stop above this bar's high on the following bar)
book_order_type: buy stop above the first close-below-MA bar's high

complexity.reason: needs the 'first occurrence since the trend began' state plus the EMA

chapter_title: Double Top Bear Flags and Double Bottom Bull Flags

name: BuyStopAboveFirstMaGapBar
quote: then buy again above the first moving average gap bar below the moving average.
description: In a strong bull trend, buy a stop above the high of the first moving-average gap bar (a bar entirely below the EMA) since the trend began.
pseudocode: isFirstMaGapBar(emaLength)
book_order_type: buy stop above the first moving-average gap bar's high

complexity.reason: needs the 'first occurrence since the trend began' state plus the EMA

chapter_title: Double Top Bear Flags and Double Bottom Bull Flags

name: SmallSignalBarWiderProtectiveStop
quote: If the signal bar is particularly small, especially if it is a doji, sometimes the entry bar will quickly reverse into an outside bar, running the protective stops ... it is often best to place your protective stop at more than one tick beyond the signal bar (maybe three ticks, but no more than a total of eight ticks from your entry
description: When the High N/Low N signal bar is small (near-doji), widen the protective stop to a few ticks beyond the signal bar's extreme instead of exactly one tick, capped at a maximum total distance from the entry price.
pseudocode: signalBarRange = high[1] - low[1]; stopOffsetTicks = (signalBarRange <= smallBarMaxTicks * tickSize) ? widerStopTicks : 1; stopPrice = max(R17-01.signalLow - stopOffsetTicks * tickSize, ctx.EntryPrice() - maxStopTicks * tickSize)
book_order_type: protective stop a few ticks beyond a small/doji signal bar, capped in total distance from entry

complexity.reason: needs the signal bar's own range plus the entry price to apply the cap

notes: The book's 8-tick cap is calibrated to the 5 minute Emini's roughly 10-point average range; treated here as a plain parameter.
chapter_title: Bar Counting: High and Low 1, 2, 3, and 4 Patterns and ABC Corrections

name: TradingRangeBreakoutStopBelowRangeLow
quote: a trader could buy the breakout on a stop and use a protective stop well below the bottom of the trading range... they need to place their protective stops far enough below the trading range so that the repeated failed downside breakouts will not stop them out.
description: For a with-trend buy on a trading-range's upside breakout, place the protective stop well below the bottom of the trading range (not just below the signal bar), to survive repeated failed downside breakout attempts before the eventual successful one.
pseudocode:
protectiveStopPrice = rangeLow - stopBufferBelowRangeLow;
exitLongOnStop = low[0] <= protectiveStopPrice;
book_order_type: protective stop order

complexity.reason: a fixed offset below a tracked range boundary; the range boundary itself is assumed already known/tracked

name: TrailingStopBelowRecentSwingLow
quote: As the trend progressed to new highs, they could have trailed their stops to below the most recent swing low. For example, after the market rallied above bar 11, their stops would then have been below bar 12, and they would have been protecting about nine points of profit.
description: As a with-trend rally progresses, trail the protective stop to just below the most recently formed swing low (mirrored: above the most recent swing high in a downtrend), tightening protection as new swing lows/highs form.
book_order_type: trailing protective stop order, moved up each time a new swing low forms

complexity.reason: needs swing-pivot detection plus a persistent trailing-stop state that only ever moves in the favorable direction

name: StopBelowPriorBarLowForSpikeEntry
quote: If the SPY traders bought at the close of that second bull trend bar, they would have put their stops below the low of the first bull trend bar (one bar earlier), and their risk would have been about 12 points.
description: For an entry taken during a strong spike (e.g., buying the close of the spike's second bar), place the initial protective stop below the low of the bar immediately preceding the entry bar.
pseudocode:
initialStopPrice = low[1] - stopBuffer;
exitLongOnStop = low[0] <= initialStopPrice;
book_order_type: protective stop order placed at entry

complexity.reason: a fixed offset from the immediately prior bar's low

name: ExitToBreakevenWhenPositionEntersTightRange
quote: If they just entered a position and the pattern grows into a tight trading range, the best option is to try to get out at breakeven or maybe with a tick loss, and then wait for the breakout before deciding on your next trade.
description: If a trade was entered before the market was recognized as a tight trading range, and the pattern has since formed, exit at breakeven (or a small loss) rather than holding for the original target.
pseudocode: exitLong = isTightTradingRange[0] && ctx.OpenPositionProfit() <= breakevenTolerance && ctx.OpenPositionProfit() >= -breakevenTolerance - smallLossAllowance;
book_order_type: market or limit exit near the entry price

complexity.reason: combines the tight-trading-range regime detector with an open-profit-near-zero test

notes: As written this only fires near breakeven; the book's fallback (hold with a wide stop) is explicitly called 'less sound' and not mechanized here (see R22-08 for a time-based alternative).

name: ExitWithTrendEntryIfRangeFailsToExpand
quote: If a trader enters with the trend in a tight trading range, expecting the trend to resume, but the market breaks out in the wrong direction, it is usually better to exit and wait for a larger trading range to develop... using a wide stop and holding for a long time is usually not a good strategy.
description: If a with-trend entry was taken while the market was a tight trading range, and after N bars the range has neither broken out with-trend nor reached a profit target, exit rather than hold through a wide stop waiting for the range to expand.
pseudocode: exitLong = isTightTradingRange[0] && ctx.BarsSinceEntry() >= maxBarsInRange && ctx.OpenPositionProfit() <= 0;
book_order_type: market exit

complexity.reason: a bar-count-since-entry time stop gated by the tight-trading-range regime and a non-positive open-profit test

notes: Same shape as the catalog's NumBarsIfLosing but additionally gated on the tight-trading-range regime; kept separate because Brooks's rationale (avoid a wide stop while waiting for range expansion) is specific to this context.

name: BreakevenStopAfterFixedFavorableMove
quote: and then to breakeven after a five-tick move, this further reduces the required winning percentage to be profitable on the day.
description: Once open profit reaches favorableTicks beyond the entry price, move the protective stop to breakeven (the entry price) for the remainder of the position.
book_order_type: stop order moved to the original entry price

complexity.reason: needs EntryPrice plus a persistent once-true flag tracking whether the favorable-move threshold has ever been reached

notes: Equivalent to ProfitProtector with maxProfit set to the dollar value of favorableTicks and retracement = 0 (exit once profit gives back to breakeven).

name: TightenStopToPriorBarLow
quote: They might raise their protective stops to one tick below the low of the current bar, even before the bar closes, and this might be only three ticks below their entry price.
description: As a trade moves favorably, Brooks has traders repeatedly move their protective stop to just beyond the most recently completed bar's extreme rather than leaving it at the original signal-bar level. Mechanized as: the position exits if the current bar trades back through the prior bar's low (long) minus a small offset, at the signal bar's close, filled at the next bar's open per the stop-exit convention.
pseudocode: close[0] <= low[1] - stopOffsetPoints
book_order_type: protective stop order placed one tick below the low of the most recently completed bar, moved forward each bar

complexity.reason: compares the current and previous bar's extreme with a fixed offset; no persistent state is kept, so it is a loose approximation of Brooks's manual ratchet (a true trail would only ever move the stop toward the trade, never away from it)

notes: Brooks describes this being done continuously and manually, sometimes intrabar ('even before the bar closes'); the close-and-next-open mechanization per MINING conventions is a simplification.

Because this only looks at low[1] rather than a persisted best-stop-so-far, the level can move down again after a pullback bar; a true monotonic trail would need cross-bar state (a 'never loosen' variable), which the authoring pass should consider as a variant.
May duplicate a swing/trail-stop primitive already mined from the Trends volume; flagging for the dedup pass rather than guessing an id.
chapter_title: Mathematics of Trading: Should I Take This Trade? Will I Make Money If I Take This Trade?

name: StopBeyondSignalBarInitialStop
quote: A reasonable location for a protective stop is at one tick above the high of the signal bar.
description: The initial protective stop for a stop-entry trade is placed stopTicks beyond the signal bar's extreme opposite the trade direction: for a long entry, stopTicks below the low of the signal bar (the bar whose breach triggered the entry, i.e. the bar immediately before the entry bar). Held until either the entry-bar tightening rule (R27-02) fires or the market moves strongly in the trade's favor.
book_order_type: protective stop order one tick beyond the signal bar's extreme

complexity.reason: needs BarsSinceEntry to locate the signal bar relative to the current bar and hold that price across bars until it is replaced

notes: Brooks's own example is a short (sell stop below the prior bar's low); the long side is the mirror as required by the pseudocode convention.

name: TightenStopAfterStrongEntryBar
quote: After the entry bar closes, if it has a strong bear body, tighten the stop to one tick above the entry bar. Otherwise, keep the stop above the signal bar until after the market begins to move strongly in your direction.
description: Once the entry bar closes, if it closed with a strong body in the trade's direction, replace the wider signal-bar stop (R27-01) with a tighter stop stopTicks beyond the entry bar's own extreme; otherwise keep the original signal-bar stop.
book_order_type: protective stop order, tightened to one tick beyond the entry bar

complexity.reason: needs BarsSinceEntry to fire exactly once after the entry bar closes, a strong-bar body test, and persistent stop-price state across the trade

notes: The strong-body test reuses the same shape as the trend-bar-body-fraction primitive used elsewhere in the corpus (e.g. rules/TrendBarBodyFraction-style pseudocode).

name: InitialStopBeyondSignalBar
quote: The initial price action stop for most trades is one tick beyond the signal bar until the entry bar closes, when it is tightened to one or two ticks beyond the entry bar if the entry bar is strong.
description: The initial protective stop for a long is placed one tick below the low of the signal bar (the bar whose close triggered the entry); for a short, one tick above its high. It stays in force until the entry bar closes.
pseudocode:
signalBarLow = low[ctx.BarsSinceEntry() + 1]; // the bar immediately before the entry bar -- still the signal bar while the entry bar has not yet closed
exitLongStop = ctx.MarketPosition() > 0 && low[0] <= signalBarLow - stopOffsetTicks * tick;
book_order_type: protective sell stop one tick below the signal bar's low (buy stop above its high for shorts)

complexity.reason: the signal bar has to be located dynamically via BarsSinceEntry() rather than a fixed lag, since the offset into history grows every bar the trade stays open

notes: Foundational stop for the whole chapter; nearly every other exit candidate here modifies or replaces this one.
Distinct from the corpus's dollar-based StopLoss: this is a price-action stop tied to a specific bar, not a fixed dollar amount.

name: TightenStopToEntryBarIfStrong
quote: The initial price action stop for most trades is one tick beyond the signal bar until the entry bar closes, when it is tightened to one or two ticks beyond the entry bar if the entry bar is strong.
description: Once the entry bar closes, if it qualified as a strong trend bar (R29-02), tighten the protective stop from beyond the signal bar to one or two ticks beyond the entry bar's own extreme instead.
pseudocode: entryBarLow = low[ctx.BarsSinceEntry()]; exitLongStop = ctx.MarketPosition() > 0 && isEntryBarStrongTrendBar[0] && ctx.BarsSinceEntry() >= 1 && low[0] <= entryBarLow - tightenOffsetTicks * tick;
book_order_type: protective sell stop moved to one or two ticks below the entry bar's low

complexity.reason: same dynamic-offset bar lookup as R29-01/R29-02, plus a dependency on the strong-trend-bar classification

notes: Replaces R29-01 once BarsSinceEntry()>=1 and the entry bar qualifies as strong; if the entry bar is a doji instead, R29-01 remains in force ('rely on your original stop').

name: SwingLowTrailingStop
quote: Since a bull trend is a series of higher highs and higher lows, it is reasonable to move the protective stop to below the most recent swing low after the market makes a new swing high. This is called a trailing stop.
description: In a trend, once the market makes a new swing high (long) / swing low (short), move the protective stop to one tick beyond the most recent confirmed swing low / high.
book_order_type: protective sell stop trailed to one tick below the most recent swing low

complexity.reason: needs swing-pivot detection to identify both the triggering new swing high and the most recent confirmed swing low used for the stop level

notes: The chapter's headline trailing-stop technique, walked through bar-by-bar in Figures 29.2 and 29.4.
Distinct from the corpus's dollar-based TrailingStop/AtrTrailingStop, which use profit peaks, not chart swing points.

name: BreakevenStopAfterHalfwayToTarget
quote: Once a swing trade reaches about halfway to the profit target, many traders will move their protective stop to break even.
description: Once the position's peak open profit has reached at least half of the trader's profit target, move the protective stop to breakeven (the entry price); exit if price then returns to breakeven.
pseudocode: reachedHalfwayToTarget = ctx.MaxPositionProfit() >= 0.5 * profitTargetDollars; exitLong = ctx.MarketPosition() > 0 && reachedHalfwayToTarget && ctx.OpenPositionProfit() <= breakevenBandDollars;
book_order_type: protective stop moved to the entry price (breakeven)

complexity.reason: needs peak-profit tracking (MaxPositionProfit, already used by the corpus's ProfitProtector family) gated by a separately defined dollar profit target

notes: Mechanically close to ProfitProtector (peak profit gives back a fraction), but the gate here is 'reached half of a fixed target' rather than 'reached a fixed floor', and the giveback is to full breakeven rather than a partial fraction.

name: StopBeyondLowestSinceEntry
quote: You also should adjust your protective stop at this point to one tick beyond that pullback, so you are now risking 12 ticks.
description: Ratchet the protective stop to one tick beyond the worst (lowest, for a long) price the market has reached since entry, once that low has held and price has resumed moving in the trade's favor.
pseudocode: worstPriceSinceEntry = lowest(low, ctx.BarsSinceEntry() + 1)[0]; exitLongStop = ctx.MarketPosition() > 0 && low[0] <= worstPriceSinceEntry - ratchetOffsetTicks * tick;
book_order_type: protective sell stop moved to one tick below the lowest low reached since entry

complexity.reason: a min/max window loop whose window length is the position's own age (BarsSinceEntry()) rather than a fixed constant

notes: Distinct from R29-05 (swing-pivot based): this uses the raw running extreme of the trade itself with no pivot detection, matching the numeric example Brooks walks through (an 11-tick pullback becomes a 12-tick stop).

name: PartialProfitNearRangeHighOnRangeTransition
quote: Once the market finally begins to enter a trading range, traders should look to take at least partial profits around the high of the range, rather than relying on their trailing stops.
description: Once price/context suggests the market is transitioning from a trend into a trading range, take partial profits near the range high rather than continuing to rely on a trailing stop.
book_order_type: limit order to take partial profits near the developing range high

complexity.reason: two independent open design questions: multi-unit/partial exits, which the engine does not model, and mechanical trading-range-transition detection

notes: Kept per the mining brief's instruction to record scaling-out candidates even though the engine only models a single all-or-nothing position.

name: DelayStopTighteningUntilProfitThreshold
quote: The stop was above the signal bar, and you should not tighten to above the high of the most recent bar until after the market had moved about four ticks in your direction or until the market had a reasonably strong bear body.
description: Do not begin tightening the bar-by-bar trailing stop until open profit has reached a minimum threshold (or a bar with a sufficiently strong body has formed in the trade's favor); before that, keep the wider initial/signal-bar stop.
pseudocode: profitThresholdReached = ctx.OpenPositionProfit() >= armTightenProfitDollars; allowStopTightening = profitThresholdReached || strongBodyInTradeDirection[0];
book_order_type: n/a (gates when other tightening rules, e.g. R29-03/R29-05, are allowed to take effect)

complexity.reason: a simple profit-threshold gate layered on top of already-defined tightening rules

notes: Modifies R29-03/R29-05: without this gate, a stop could tighten too early on a single strong-looking bar not yet backed by real profit.

name: WideStopSizedToBreakoutRun

name: BreakevenExitAtOriginalEntryAfterScaling
